rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier forgot that God first made him from a lifeless drop and assembled life in him.
rows.anchor: أي ونسي أنا أنشأناه من نطفة ميتة فركبنا فيه الحياة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet answers the objector that God will resurrect him and enter him into the Fire.
rows.anchor:
قال عليه السلام:
" نعم ويبعثك الله ويدخلك النار "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves the soundness of analogical reasoning: God argues for resurrection from the first creation.
rows.anchor: ففي هذا دليل على صحة القياس لأن الله جل وعز احتج على منكري البعث بالنشأة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramīm means decayed; the bone is called ramīm or ramām when it has crumbled away.
rows.anchor: رم العظم فهو رميم ورمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramīm is masculine because it is shifted from the feminine fāʿila form; likewise بغيا drops its feminine ending as shifted from باغية.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال رميم ولم يقل رميمة لأنها معدولة عن فاعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unbeliever asked the Prophet whether God could restore bones if he crushed and scattered them in the wind; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن هذا الكافر قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who originated the bones from nothing can restore them in the second creation from the remaining tailbone.
rows.anchor: أي من غير شيء فهو قادر على إعادتها في النشأة الثانية من شيء وهو عجم الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tailbone is called ʿajm al-dhanab, with an alternate spelling ʿajb using bāʾ.
rows.anchor: ويقال عجب الذنب بالباء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows how to originate and how to restore every creation.
rows.anchor: أي كيف يبدىء ويعيد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وبعض أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and some Shafiʿi associates hold that bones have life and become impure at death.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي حنيفة وبعض أصحاب الشافعي

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds that bones have no life, differing from Abu Hanifa and some of his own associates.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه: لا حياة فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion that bones means their owners by an omitted possessive is unnecessary; no ellipsis is needed here.
rows.anchor: قلنا: إنما يكون إذا احتيج لضرورة وليس هاهنا ضرورة تدعو إلى هذا الإضمار

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says sensory perception, a sign of life, is present in bones, supporting the literal reading.
rows.anchor: فإن الإحساس الذي هو علامة الحياة موجود فيه قاله ابن العربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is accusative with the sense of min an, from the fact that a warner came to them.
rows.anchor: «أن» في موضع نصب والمعنى من أن جاءهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing connects their astonishment to the preceding description of pride and discord, with the destruction phrase parenthetical.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو متصل بقوله: { في عزة وشقاق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate reading begins a new statement: their astonishment at a warner from among them displays their ignorance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا بل هذا ابتداء كلام أي ومن جهلهم أنهم أظهروا التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him a magician means that his deceptive speech tricks people.
rows.anchor: أي يجيء بالكلام المموه الذي يخدع به الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate explanation is that they called him a magician because his magic separated parent from child and husband from wife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يفرق بسحره بين الوالد وولده والرجل وزوجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called him a liar in his claim to prophethood.
rows.anchor: أي في دعوى النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb has two objects: make the many gods into one god.
rows.anchor: مفعولان أي صير الآلهة إلها واحدا

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulami reads ʿujāb with a doubled jīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: «عجاب» بالتشديد.

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil distinguishes ʿajīb as amazing from ʿujāb as exceeding the ordinary limit of wonder, as ṭawīl differs from ṭuwāl.
rows.anchor: وقد فرق الخليل بين عجيب وعجاب فقال: العجيب العجب، والعجاب الذي قد تجاوز حد العجب

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari defines ʿajīb as something marvellous and says doubled ʿujāb is more emphatic than the other forms.
rows.anchor: وقال الجوهري: العجيب الأمر الذي يتعجب منه، وكذلك العجاب بالضم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies ʿujāb as a dialect word of Azd Shanuʾa.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: «عجاب» لغة أزد شنوءة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that during Abu Talib’s illness Quraysh asked the Prophet’s aim; he sought one monotheistic word that would bring Arab submission and non-Arab tribute, prompting their objection and revelation of verses 38:4-7. Al-Tirmidhi also narrates it by meaning and grades it hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Quraysh approached Abu Talib after Umar converted, asking him to settle matters; they offered to leave the Prophet and his God if he abandoned their idols. He proposed one word that would rule Arabia and bring non-Arabs under their religion; Abu Jahl accepted even tenfold, but they recoiled at monotheism.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: «أجعل الآلهة إلها واحدا» فكيف يسع الخلق كلهم إله واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection asks how one god could suffice for all creatures; God revealed these verses through the mention of Noah’s people.
rows.anchor: فكيف يسع الخلق كلهم إله واحد. فأنزل الله فيهم هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ means the notables, and inṭilāq is going away quickly; the unbelievers left the Prophet urging one another to continue as before.
rows.anchor: «الملأ» الأشراف، والانطلاق الذهاب بسرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their instruction is to keep to their former way, avoid Muhammad’s religion, and persevere in worshipping their gods.
rows.anchor: أي امضوا على ما كنتم عليه ولا تدخلوا في دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate account takes their departure as their visit to Abu Talib during his illness, described earlier.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو إشارة إلى مشيهم إلى أبي طالب في مرضه كما سبق

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the visitors to Abu Talib as Abu Jahl, Shayba and ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Umayya ibn Khalaf, al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil, and Abu Muʿayt; they demanded he stop his nephew and his followers.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية محمد بن إسحاق أنهم أبو جهل بن هشام، وشيبة وعتبة أبناء ربيعة بن عبد شمس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is accusative here with an implied bi: they departed by saying, Go on.
rows.anchor: { أن امشوا } في موضع نصب والمعنى بأن امشوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an means ay; the phrase explains what their departure amounted to, rather than quoting words they literally spoke.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «أن» بمعنى أي أي «وانطلق الملأ منهم» أي امشوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account has the nobles telling the common people to go on and remain steadfast in worship of their gods.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى انطلق الأشراف منهم فقالوا للعوام: «امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that something is intended for the people of the earth: their people’s blessings will be removed and calamity will befall them.
rows.anchor: أي يراد بأهل الأرض من زوال نعم قوم وغير تنزل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they warn that Muhammad wants submission so he can dominate and control them, and urge people not to obey him.
rows.anchor: كلمة تحذير أي إنما يريد محمد بما يقول الانقياد له ليعلو علينا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Quraysh called Umar’s conversion a thing intended because it strengthened Islam and distressed them.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إن عمر لما أسلم وقوي به الإسلام شق ذلك على قريش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والقرظي وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Qurazi, Qatada, Muqatil, al-Kalbi, and al-Suddi take the last religion to mean Christianity, whose adherents associate another god with God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والقرظي وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي والسدي: يعنون ملة عيسى النصرانية

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and, in another report, Qatada say the phrase means the religion of Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة أيضا: يعنون ملة قريش.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan understands them to mean that they had never heard such a thing would happen at the end of time.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما سمعنا أن هذا يكون في آخر الزمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they had not heard from the People of the Book that Muhammad was a true messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي ما سمعنا من أهل الكتاب أن محمدا رسول حق.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain ikhtilāq as a lie or fabrication; khalaqa and ikhtalaqa mean to invent.
rows.anchor: يقال: خلق واختلق أي ابتدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related verb is also used of God creating creatures by originating them without a prior model.
rows.anchor: وخلق الله عز وجل الخلق من هذا أي ابتدعهم على غير مثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr here is the Quran; they objected that revelation had singled him out, although they knew he had always been truthful and only doubted whether the revelation came from God.
rows.anchor: والذكر هاهنا القرآن. أنكروا اختصاصه بالوحي من بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase from the stream story, Whoever drank of it is not of me, means not of my religion and way.
rows.anchor: فمن شرب منه فليس مني

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads them as a defeated host, barred from ascending to heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى هم جند مغلوب أي ممنوع عن أن يصعد إلى السماء.

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says they are a host defeated for the idols: neither the idols nor the host can obtain anything from God’s treasuries of mercy or dominion.
rows.anchor: وقال القتبي: يعني أنهم جند لهذه الآلهة مهزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharḥ means opening and making spacious.
rows.anchor: شرح فتح ووسع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God widened the person’s breast to Islam until it became firm within him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وسع صدره للإسلام حتى ثبت فيه.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Islam expanded the breast through joy and tranquility; on this reading, the expansion follows Islam, whereas Ibn Abbas’s reading allows it to precede it.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: وسع صدره بالإسلام للفرح به والطمأنينة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being on light means being guided by God, in contrast with one whose heart is sealed and hardened.
rows.anchor: أي على هدى من ربه كمن طبع على قلبه وأقساه

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says qasā means becoming hard; ʿatā and ʿasā are close in meaning, and a hard heart does not soften.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: يقال قسا القلب إذا صلب، وكذلك عتا وعسا مقاربة لها.

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators identify the person whose breast was expanded as ʿAli and Hamza.
rows.anchor: والمراد بمن شرح الله صدره هاهنا فيما ذكر المفسرون علي وحمزة

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash reports that the referent is Umar ibn al-Khattab.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش أنه عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the referent as ʿAmmar ibn Yasir.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: عمار بن ياسر.

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Muqatil also reports, together with al-Kalbi, that the referent is the Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا والكلبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse applies generally to anyone in whose heart God creates faith and thereby expands the breast.
rows.anchor: والآية عامة فيمن شرح الله صدره بخلق الإيمان فيه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from Ibn Masud, the Prophet says light entering the heart opens it; its signs are turning to the eternal home, detaching from delusion, and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قلنا يا رسول الله قوله تعالى: { أفمن شرح الله صدره

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim’s Nawadir al-Usul from Ibn Umar calls the wisest believer one who remembers death most and prepares best; it repeats that light opens the heart and lists the same three signs.
rows.anchor: وخرجه الترمذي الحكيم في «نوادر الأصول» من حديث ابن عمر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three signs mark complete faith: inabah consists of good works because the eternal home is their reward.
rows.anchor: فذكر صلى الله عليه وسلم خصالا ثلاث، ولا شك أن من كانت فيه هذه الخصال فهو الكامل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is the reward for deeds, as God says in the verse cited here.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى كيف ذكره الله في مواضع في تنزيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant turns toward the eternal home by persisting in good works; detachment means curbing worldly desire, accepting what suffices, and being content.
rows.anchor: فإذا انكمش العبد في أعمال البر فهو إنابته إلى دار الخلود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readiness for death means acting with taqwa, deliberation, caution, and scrupulous avoidance of doubtful matters; these are outward signs.
rows.anchor: وإذا أحكم أموره بالتقوى فكان ناظرا في كل أمر، واقفا متأدبا متثبتا حذرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs arise from seeing death and the afterlife as displacing the deceptive world; that vision comes through light entering the heart.
rows.anchor: وإنما صار هكذا لرؤية الموت، ورؤية صرف الآخرة عن الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the hard-hearted as Abu Lahab and his children.
rows.anchor: قيل: المراد أبو لهب وولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, hearing God’s remembrance makes their hearts even harder.
rows.anchor: ومعنى: «من ذكر الله» أن قلوبهم تزداد قسوة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari takes min to mean ʿan: their hearts hardened against accepting God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن «من» بمعنى عن، والمعنى قست عن قبول ذكر الله. وهذا اختيار الطبري.

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In a report from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, God says to seek needs from generous people, who contain His mercy, rather than hard-hearted people, who contain His anger.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى اطلبوا الحوائج من السمحاء فإني جعلت فيهم رحمتي

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no punishment is greater than a hardened heart, and that God removes mercy from a people when angry with them.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: ما ضرب عبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best hadith is the Quran: after speaking of following the best, God clarifies that the best thing heard is what He revealed.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن لما قال: { فيتبعون أحسنه } بين أن أحسن ما يسمع ما أنزله الله

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Saʿd reports that companions asked for stories and reminders; the Quran’s best-stories verse and the call to humility before God’s remembrance followed.
rows.anchor: قال سعد بن أبي وقاص قال أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the companions grew weary and asked the Prophet to tell them something, after which this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملوا ملة فقالوا له:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadith is what a narrator relates; the Quran is called hadith because the Prophet used to tell it to his companions and people, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: والحديث ما يحدث به المحدث. وسمى القرآن حديثا

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri rejects the inference that hadith here means created divine speech: newness applies to recitation, not what is recited, like remembrance in relation to God’s remembered names.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري: وتوهم قوم أن الحديث من الحدوث فليدل على أن كلامه محدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāban can be an appositive to ahsan al-hadith or a circumstantial accusative describing it.
rows.anchor: { كتابا } نصب على البدل من «أحسن الحديث»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran resembles itself in beauty and wisdom, confirms itself, and contains no contradiction or disagreement.
rows.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا في الحسن والحكمة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Quran’s verses and letters resemble one another.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: يشبه بعضه بعضا في الآي والحروف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says it resembles the scriptures sent to earlier prophets in its commands, prohibitions, encouragement, and warnings, while being broader and inimitable.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يشبه كتب الله المنزلة على أنبيائه لما يتضمنه من أمر ونهي وترغيب وترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathānī refers to repeated stories, admonitions, and rulings; the text is doubled in recitation so it does not become tiresome.
rows.anchor: تثنى فيه القصص والمواعظ والأحكام وثني للتلاوة فلا يمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqshaʿirru means to tremble and shiver in fear of the warnings it contains.
rows.anchor: تضطرب وتتحرك بالخوف مما فيه من الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their skins and hearts soften toward God’s remembrance when they hear a verse of mercy.
rows.anchor: أي عند آية الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, softening toward remembrance means acting according to God’s book and affirming it, or turning to Islam.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى العمل بكتاب الله والتصديق به. وقيل: «إلى ذكر الله» يعني الإسلام.

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Asma says the Prophet’s companions wept and shivered as God describes when Quran was recited; she sought refuge from Satan when told that people now faint at recitation.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنهما قالت: كان أصحاب النبي

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Rahman al-Jumahi reports that Ibn Umar saw a Quran reciter collapsed; he said they feared God without collapsing and suspected Satan’s influence, unlike the Prophet’s companions.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن عبد الرحمن الجمحي: مر ابن عمر برجل من أهل القرآن ساقط

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin challenges claims of Quran-induced fainting: have the person sit on a roof with legs out and recite the whole Quran; if he throws himself down, he is truthful.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز: ذكر عند ابن سيرين الذين يصرعون إذا قرىء عليهم القرآن

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni recounts that after Moses preached to Israel and a man tore his shirt, God told Moses to forbid wasteful tearing and ask the man to open his heart to Him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمران الجوني: وعظ موسى عليه السلام بني إسرائيل ذات يوم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb recited before the Prophet and companions became tender; the Prophet said to seize the moment for supplication because it is mercy.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم: قرأ أبي بن كعب عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعه أصحابه فرقوا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from al-Abbas says that when a believer’s skin shivers from fear of God, sins fall away like leaves from a withered tree.
rows.anchor: وعن العباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says that God forbids the Fire to any servant whose skin shivers from fear of Him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: أم الدرداء
rows.claim: Umm al-Darda compares fear in a person’s heart to a burning palm frond and says shivering is a cue to pray, when supplication is answered.
rows.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب عن أم الدرداء قالت:

rows.speaker: فلان
rows.claim: Thabit al-Bunani quotes an unnamed person who recognizes answered prayer when his skin shivers, heart fears, and eyes overflow.
rows.anchor: وعن ثابت البناني قال قال فلان: إني لأعلم متى يستجاب لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb has the verbal noun iqshiʿrār and participle muqshaʿirr; its plural qashāʿir drops the extra mīm, and the state is called qashʿarīra.
rows.anchor: يقال: اقشعر جلد الرجل اقشعرارا فهو مقشعر

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays’s line uses muqshaʿirr for the heart shivering in fear, illustrating the word’s usage.
rows.anchor:
قال امرؤ القيس:
فبت أكابد ليل التما
م والقلب من خشية مقشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Quran’s unmatched eloquence makes listeners’ skins shiver: they recognize their inability to rival it and feel awe at its arrangement and content.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن القرآن لما كان في غاية الجزالة والبلاغة، فكانوا إذا رأوا عجزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shivering and softening are compared to the mountain humbled and split from fear of God in the cited verse; splitting is close to shivering and humility to softening.
rows.anchor: وهو كقوله تعالى: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart’s softening means tenderness, calm, and tranquility.
rows.anchor: ومعنى لين القلب رقته وطمأنينته وسكونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That guidance refers to the Quran as God’s guidance.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن هدى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fear of punishment and hope for reward that God grants these people is His guidance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي الذي وهبه الله لهؤلاء من خشية عقابه ورجاء ثوابه

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God abandons has no guide; this statement refutes the Qadariyya and others.
rows.anchor: أي من خذله فلا مرشد له. وهو يرد على القدرية وغيرهم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin pronounce the final yāʾ when pausing on hād in both locations; the other readers omit it.
rows.anchor: ووقف ابن كثير وابن محيصن على قوله: «هاد» في الموضعين بالياء، الباقون بغير ياء.

rows.speaker: عطاء وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ata and Ibn Zayd say the person is thrown shackled into the Fire, with its first contact on his face.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء وابن زيد: يرمى به مكتوفا في النار فأول شيء تمس منه النار وجهه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the person is dragged face-first through the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يجر على وجهه في النار.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil pictures a disbeliever thrown into the Fire with hands chained to the neck and a mountain-sized sulfur rock hanging there; it burns and scorches the face, which the chains prevent him from shielding.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هو أن الكافر يرمى به في النار مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause has an omitted predicate or comparison.
rows.anchor: والخبر محذوف

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies the comparison: is one who wards off punishment with his face better, or one who is fortunate, as in the cited verse?
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: أي { أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب } أفضل أم من سعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are disbelievers, and their keepers address them in rebuke and reproach.
rows.anchor: أي وتقول الخزنة للكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to taste the recompense for what they earned through sins.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء كسبكم من المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is paralleled by the command to taste what was hoarded in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: هذا ما كنزتم لأنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier deniers were unexpectedly punished and humiliated in worldly life; the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they knew.
rows.anchor: أي مما أصابهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says anything reaching a body part is said to be tasted, by analogy with sweetness or bitterness reaching the taster.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: يقال لكل ما نال الجارحة من شيء قد ذاقته

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad distinguishes al-khizyu, harm or disgrace, from al-khizāya, shame.
rows.anchor: قال: والخزي من المكروه والخزاية من الاستحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ in kāfin is dropped before the following tanwin; although it could be restored at pause, it stays dropped to match connected pronunciation, while some Arabs say kāfī at pause.
rows.anchor: حذفت الياء من «كاف» لسكونها وسكون التنوين بعدها

rows.speaker: عامة القراء
rows.claim: The common reading is singular, referring to Muhammad, whom God protects from the threats and plots of the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة { عبده } بالتوحيد يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the plural ʿibādahu, referring either to the prophets or to the prophets and their believers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { عباده } وهم الأنبياء أو الأنبياء والمؤمنون بهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the common singular reading because the next clause addresses the Prophet directly.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد قراءة الجماعة لقوله عقيبه: { ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular may be generic, like al-insān in the cited verse, making the first reading include the plural sense.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون العبد لفظ الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God suffices against the harm of idols, with which the polytheists frightened believers; Abraham made the same argument in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: والكفاية شر الأصنام، فإنهم كانوا يخوفون المؤمنين بالأصنام

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani says God suffices His believing servant through reward and His unbelieving servant through punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال الجرجاني: إن الله كاف عبده المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threatened the Prophet with harm from idols, saying that unless he stopped speaking against them they would maim or hurt him.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم خوفوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مضرة الأوثان، فقالوا: أتسب آلهتنا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that Khalid ibn al-Walid went to break al-ʿUzza with an axe; its caretaker warned him, but Khalid smashed its nose.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: مشى خالد بن الوليد إلى العزى ليكسرها بالفأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to Khalid also counts as a threat to the Prophet because the Prophet had sent Khalid.
rows.anchor: وتخويفهم لخالد تخويف للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه الذي وجه خالدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat also includes frightening the Prophet with their numbers and strength, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: ويدخل في الآية تخويفهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بكثرة جمعهم وقوتهم

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that one whom God misguides has no guide was explained earlier.
rows.anchor: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

words: وَمَن يَهْدِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّضِلٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can mislead a person God guides; God is mighty and exacts vengeance on those who oppose Him or His messengers.
rows.anchor: أي ممن عاداه أو عادى رسله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says this verse was revealed concerning Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: قيل: إنها نزلت في حذيفة بن المغيرة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the person claims to have received the blessing through his own knowledge of ways to earn money.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: { على علم } عندي بوجوه المكاسب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada also reports an interpretation that the speaker means he received it because of good fortune he possesses.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا { على علم } على خير عندي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the speaker claims God knows his merit and therefore gave him the blessing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: { على علم } أي على علم من الله بفضلي.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the speaker means he received it through knowledge God taught him.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: { على علم } أي بعلم علمني الله إياه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the person thinks his worldly allotment shows that he holds a rank with God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أنه قال قد علمت أني إذا أوتيت هذا في الدنيا أن لي عند الله منزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God corrects him: the blessings given are a trial by which he is tested.
rows.anchor: فقال الله: { بل هي فتنة } أي بل النعم التي أوتيتها فتنة تختبر بها.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says hi is feminine because fitnah is feminine, though huwa fitnah would also be grammatical.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: أنث «هي» لتأنيث الفتنة، ولو كان بل هو فتنة لجاز.

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas supplies the omitted wording: rather, I gave it to him as a trial.
rows.anchor: النحاس: التقدير بل أعطيته فتنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not understand that being given wealth is a test.
rows.anchor: أي لا يعلمون أن إعطاءهم المال اختبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine ending in qālahā agrees with the feminine noun kalimah, understood in the wording.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قد قالها } أنث على تأنيث الكلمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those before them are earlier unbelievers, including Qarun, who made the same claim about his knowledge.
rows.anchor: يعني الكفار قبلهم كقارون وغيره حيث قال: «إنما أوتيته على علم عندي».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the negative reading of mā, their wealth and children did not protect them from God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: «ما» للجحد أي لم تغن عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من عذاب الله شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā is interrogative: what did their wealth benefit them?
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي فما الذي أغنى أموالهم؟ ف«ما» استفهام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They suffered the recompense for their evil deeds; the punishment may itself be called an evil deed.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء سيئات أعمالهم. وقد يسمى جزاء السيئة سيئة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers among this community are those who associate partners with God; they will suffer famine and the sword.
rows.anchor: أي أشركوا { من هؤلاء } الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot escape God or get ahead of Him.
rows.anchor: أي فائتين الله ولا سابقيه

words: أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands and constricts provision for whomever He wills; this is a sign for people who believe.
rows.anchor: أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are singled out because they reflect on the signs and benefit from them.
rows.anchor: خص المؤمن بالذكر لأنه هو الذي يتدبر الآيات وينتفع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An abundance of provision can be a plot and gradual entrapment, while restricting provision may elevate and honor a person.
rows.anchor: ويعلم أن سعة الرزق قد يكون مكرا واستدراجا، وتقتيره رفعة وإعظاما.

words: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes each soul receiving its due: unbelievers are driven to the Fire and believers to Paradise.
rows.anchor: هذا بيان توفية كل نفس عملها، فيساق الكافر إلى النار والمؤمن إلى الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zumar means groups; its singular zumrah has the same pattern relation as ẓulmah to ghurfah in the cited forms.
rows.anchor: والزمر: الجماعات واحدتها زمرة كظلمة وغرفة.

rows.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubayda explain zumar as separate groups following one after another.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش وأبو عبيدة: { زمرا } جماعات متفرقة بعضها إثر بعض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s line describes people visiting a man’s dwelling in groups, one group after another.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
وترى الناس إلى منزله
زمرا تنتابه بعد زمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second unnamed poet also says that groups follow one another in succession.
rows.anchor:
وقال آخر:
حتى احزألت
زمر بعد زمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss takes the word to mean that they are pushed and driven with a sound like a mizmar.
rows.anchor: وقيل: دفعا وزجرا بصوت كصوت المزمار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to when they arrive is that the gates open, and there are seven gates, as discussed in Surat al-Hijr.
rows.anchor: جواب إذا، وهي سبعة أبواب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers’ singular is khāzin, just as sadanah is the plural of sādin; they speak in reproach and reprimand.
rows.anchor: واحدهم خازن نحو سدنة وسادن، يقولون لهم تقريعا وتوبيخا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord’s signs recited by the messengers are the scriptures revealed to the prophets.
rows.anchor: أي الكتب المنزلة على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To warn them means to frighten them about the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا بلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their yes is an admission that messengers came and that the proof had been established against them.
rows.anchor: أي قد جاءتنا، وهذا اعتراف منهم بقيام الحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The binding word of punishment is God’s declaration that He will fill Hell with jinn and people together.
rows.anchor:
وهي قوله تعالى:
لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين
[هود: 119]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to enter the gates of Hell means that they are told to enter Hell.
rows.anchor: أي يقال لهم ادخلوا جهنم

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the guards meet them with fiery clubs and drive them; one blow sends into the Fire as many people as the tribes of Rabiʿa and Mudar.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: تستقبلهم الزبانية بمقامع من نار فيدفعونهم بمقامعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concludes that Hell is a wretched resting place for the arrogant.
rows.anchor: فبئس مثوى المتكبرين } تقدم بيانه.
